source: FAO/OIE/World Bank, "Good Practices for Biosecurity in the Pig Sector - Issues and Options in Developing and Transition Countries", FAO Animal Production and Health Paper No. 169, Rome, 2010.
text: Manure from infected pigs can carry large quantities of pathogens, including parasites and bacteria such as Salmonella and Campylobacter species, and can introduce disease into the human food chain if spread on agricultural land or into fish ponds without adequate treatment or care during storage and spreading. Bedding materials such as sawdust or wood shavings can also carry pathogens if sourced from a contaminated location. This is a relevant caution for integrated pig-fish-vegetable farming systems common in Cambodia, where pig manure is often deliberately used as pond or garden fertilizer - the practice is valuable but should not use manure from visibly sick animals.
